title: MarkdownMinimap never draws when its content mounts after it
foundBy: an independent reviewer agent, one of three asked whether each component specification still describes the component that exists

evidence.verified: A browser test mounts the minimap first and the content second, which is the shape the record describes. Against the component as it stood, it painted 0 pixels of canvas after the content arrived and 600ms passed. With the element as the prop it paints 82610. The test is kept as a regression guard, and freezing the dependencies back to something that does not change when the content arrives fails it again with `expected 0 to be greater than 0`. `npm run ci` exits 0 with every gate run, 636 tests, visual:compare 104/104 at 0 differing pixels, axe 0, and docs:compile accepts the rewritten example.

details:
`components/MarkdownMinimap.md:97` says the initial draw timeout covers the case where the content mounts after the minimap.

It cannot. `src/components/MarkdownMinimap.tsx:98` returns from the effect when `contentRef.current` is empty, and the `setTimeout` that would schedule the draw sits below it at `:105`. The effect's dependencies are `[contentRef, drawMinimap]` at `:128`, and a ref object does not change identity when its `current` is populated later.

So the effect never runs a second time. A consumer who mounts the minimap before its content gets a permanently blank canvas, with no scroll listener and no resize observer attached.

notes.text: Session agent confirmed every citation in this record against the tree at a374f2c before filing it.

The owner chose the API change over the smaller fix, having asked for the right behaviour rather than the cheapest one. Both were built and measured first. Mirroring the element into state kept the prop and fixed the case in nine lines, but it works by re-checking on every render, so it depends on the component being called again after the element appears. That holds when one state change drives both, and not when a consumer memoises the minimap. Taking the element makes the arrival itself the trigger, so nothing has to notice.

Breaking, and deliberately so at 0.2.0. Three call sites moved with it: MarkdownViewer, which now mirrors its scroller node into state alongside the ref it still reads, and two tests. A consumer changes `contentRef={ref}` to `content={element}` with `ref={setElement}` on the content, and the compiler names every site rather than failing silently. No other component in the library keys an effect on a ref prop, checked across `src/components/`.
